scope: Independent read-only source review of exactly two new Kotlin sources; no test rerun, no new synthesis or Android playback
checks: Main Handler owns player/generation/state; public actions post there. Actual bridge synthesis completion returns via its main Handler, so its success/error callbacks preserve that ownership.

PCM parsing alone runs on a bounded single worker. Generation, active and destroyed are rechecked on the posted completion. Stop increments generation before cancel callbacks, cancels envelope work and closes data/player.
MediaPlayer is created on main; progress uses its actual currentPosition and duration, not elapsed wall time. Rate changes therefore keep sample timing attached to media position.
Mute/zero stream volume and inactive/destroyed states publish zero envelope. These are software playback conditions, not evidence of an audible physical speaker.

PCM16 RIFF parser bounds bytes/chunk counts/duration/alignment, rejects unsupported/truncated data and detects worker interruption. Unsupported envelope data yields EMPTY rather than synthesized motion.
Original game==learning, voiceEnabled and local-license requirements remain. No online request, microphone or child-progress write was added.
20ms RMS amplitudes with fixed art gain describe loudness only, not phonemes, visemes or linguistic synchronization.
Actual original engine pcmWave writes mono little-endian signed PCM16 at44100Hz, matching the production profile consumed by this adapter.

existing_logs_read_only.kind: Synthetic JVM boundary contracts; not an Android sound run

limits: No Android MediaPlayer lifecycle or audible-speaker acceptance performed by this reviewer.
No claim about a rendered mouth, expressive quality, phoneme synchronization or physical device FPS.
The parser accepts other PCM rates, but the reviewed production engine emits44100Hz.
